old: Two established bodies of literature motivate this functional form. The multiplicative wedge (1 + λij) on delivered cost is the standard representation of ad valorem bilateral trade frictions in the gravity literature (Anderson and van Wincoop 2003), where pair-specific wedges capture border effects, policy barriers, and non-tariff measures that raise the price paid by buyer j for seller i’s services above the seller’s own cost. The linear additive structure of the two components Gij and Rij treats geopolitical, regulatory, and sanctions frictions as separable contributions to the wedge, consistent with the iceberg-equivalent decomposition of services trade costs in Benz and Jaax (2020).
